body.text: CHALLENGE 3/5 - HANDSHAKE, KEY SEPARATION, NONCES. Three coupled decisions. (a) Static-static X25519 gives no forward secrecy and no cross-session key separation; a signed ephemeral handshake (Ed25519 identity key signs an X25519 ephemeral pubkey, 2 messages) costs ~30 lines and gives authentication plus FS. Do we do signed-ephemeral, or accept static-static with a transcript salt and list forward secrecy as an explicit non-goal in my non-goals doc? (b) HKDF MUST derive TWO directional keys (K_a2b, K_b2a) with distinct info labels, or the two peers reuse the same key+nonce space and Poly1305 forgery becomes trivial. Confirm directional keys. (c) I propose deterministic nonces: 4-byte direction/epoch prefix || 8-byte big-endian seq, reusing the replay counter, so nonce reuse becomes a detectable invariant violation instead of a birthday-bound gamble, with hard fail-closed at seq overflow. Random 96-bit nonces are the alternative. Which?
